lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Supervised application: voter registration and civic participation in outline

objective: Learners research the actual eligibility requirements and general registration process for voting where they live, note when they personally would become eligible, and complete a provided fictional practice form to understand the kind of information the real process asks for, without submitting anything or taking any real registration action.
scenario: The learner researches the real eligibility rules (age and any other requirement) and the general outline of the registration process for their own location from a current source, records when they personally would become eligible, and fills out a provided fictional practice form modeled on a typical registration form to see what information it actually asks for.
safetyNotes: This lesson is research and outline only; no real registration, submission, or account signup happens as part of this task.
The practice form is fictional and provided with this lesson; it is filled out for understanding only and is not a real government document.
This lesson presents the general process neutrally and does not advocate for any candidate, party, or position.
materials: access to research real local voter eligibility and registration rules, or the provided reference summary

tasks.directions: Before researching, write what you currently know or assume about voter eligibility rules.

prompts.text: Write your current assumptions about who is eligible to register to vote and when.

tasks.directions: Research the actual eligibility requirements and general registration outline for your location, and record when you personally would become eligible.

prompts.text: Record the actual eligibility requirements you found and the general outline of the registration process, naming your source.
State when you personally would become eligible based on what you found.

tasks.directions: Fill out the provided fictional practice form to see what kind of information the real process actually asks for.

prompts.text: I completed the fictional practice form using only the placeholder information it provides, not any of my own real personal details.
Name one piece of information the practice form asks for that surprised you.

tasks.directions: Reflect on civic participation more broadly.

prompts.text: Beyond voting, name one other way someone your age can genuinely participate in civic life right now, based on what you found.

remediation: If a learner's eligibility research is vague or based on assumption rather than a verified current source, reteach by requiring the source to be named explicitly and by having the learner state their own eligibility date as a specific calculation from that source's stated rule.
extension: Have the learner research one local civic activity open to their current age group (such as a youth council or a community meeting) and describe what participating would actually involve.
